title: Multi-tenant priority queueing for audit webhook relay with per-tenant delivery guarantees
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background: Our audit-relay currently uses a single FIFO worker pool that treats all tenants equally. Under load bursts from a few noisy tenants we observe dropped or delayed webhook deliveries to SIEM sinks (Splunk/Datadog/third-party webhooks). This increases operational toil, causes missed alerts for some customers, and makes SLA promises brittle.

Goal: Implement a multi-tenant priority queueing layer in the audit webhook relay that enforces per-tenant SLO classes (gold/silver/bronze), prevents noisy-tenant head-of-line blocking, and preserves per-tenant delivery guarantees: ordering for ordered sinks, at-least-once delivery with deduplication tokens, and bounded retry/backoff behavior. Integrate this with existing DLQ, per-tenant rate quotas, and observability so Support and SRE can quickly diagnose delivery issues.

Scope: Design and implement the queueing and scheduling layer, metadata and checkpoints for per-tenant progress, idempotency token enforcement, and integration adapters for Splunk/Datadog/SIEM webhooks. Excludes storage-tier changes for long-term archival which will be handled in a follow-up.

Non-goal: Changing audit event schema or customer-facing webhook payloads except for adding a mandatory delivery metadata envelope for retries/signing.
acceptance_criteria: Support three tenant SLO classes (gold/silver/bronze) configurable per-tenant in the Console and via API

Under synthetic noisy-tenant load, gold tenants sustain 99.9% timely delivery (defined as webhook POST accepted by sink within per-tenant SLA) while bronze tenants may see degraded throughput but no system-wide collapse
Ordering-preserving mode: for sinks that require ordering, events for a tenant must be delivered in sequence and retries must not result in reordering
Idempotency: repeated deliveries include idempotency tokens and the relay plus connectors ensure at-least-once semantics without duplicate application for supported sinks
Backpressure and DLQ: when a tenant exceeds retry budget or sink signals unrecoverable error, events for that tenant move to a tenant-scoped DLQ with audit trail
Observability: dashboards showing per-tenant queue depth, head-of-line latency, retry rates, and number of events in DLQ
Configurable tenant quotas enforceable at relay ingress and queue scheduler
Security: payload signing and optional per-tenant shared secret support for webhook integrations, documented and covered by security review
implementation_notes: Introduce an in-memory priority-scheduler with pluggable backing: Redis streams for durability+checkpointing, fallback to local buffered queues for low-latency paths
Queueing keys per tenant+route, with priority weight derived from tenant SLO class and recent error history (adaptive deprioritization)
Per-tenant sliding-window counters to enforce quotas and to calculate dynamic backoff windows
Idempotency metadata: every audit event forwarded to sinks carry a stable delivery_id (UUIDv1) and sequence_number for ordering sinks; connectors must honor delivery_id to dedupe
Checkpoint model: store last-acked sequence_number per tenant per-route in Redis with expiration and persistent snapshot to the audit event store to enable replay
Retry policy: configurable retry budgets and exponential backoff with jitter; support immediate short-circuit for gold tenants when holding capacity
DLQ semantics: tenant-scoped DLQs in object storage with manifest entries, plus a small in-heap DLQ for fast inspection in Console
Connector adapters: Splunk HEC and Datadog intake wrappers to translate envelope, sign payloads using per-tenant secrets, and surface sink-specific errors to scheduler for adaptive handling
Resource isolation: worker pools with soft CPU/GPU (if used for signing) admission controls per priority tier
Security: integrate with RBAC v2 so Console config changes require admin role; store per-tenant webhook secrets in KMS/HSM and never log raw secrets
Feature flags: gate new scheduler behind a runtime feature flag and Console toggle to fall back to legacy FIFO
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests and integration tests in sandbox, feature flag off by default
Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal test tenants (10%) and run synthetic noisy-tenant scenarios; validate metrics and rollback if head-of-line latency increases for gold tenants
Phase 2 (early customers): opt-in for customers wanting higher SLAs (up to 5 customers), collect feedback and tweak quotas
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 25% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 3 weeks with automated health checks
Rollback criteria: sustained increase >10% in gold tenant 95th latency or >5% rise in delivery error rate over a 30-minute window
Migration: ensure ability to replay events from legacy queue to new scheduler using snapshot/sequence checkpointing during migration window
testing_plan: Unit tests for scheduler logic (priority ordering, starvation prevention, adaptive deprioritization)
Integration tests: end-to-end from audit producer -> relay -> Splunk/Datadog mock sink with induced failures (timeouts, 5xx, network drops)
Performance: load test with 10k tenants and 1M events/hour measuring memory, latency, and throughput; verify gold tenants meet SLO
Chaos tests: random worker restarts, Redis failover, KMS latency spikes, and DLQ durability tests
Security tests: secret rotation, signature verification failures, RBAC restriction tests on Console config changes
Regression: run existing delivery guarantee test-suite to confirm no regressions in DLQ behavior and ordering guarantees
security_considerations: Per-tenant webhook secrets stored in KMS; reference keys in config so code never sees raw secret
Signed payloads (HMAC-SHA256) mandatory for enterprise customers; include signature header and delivery metadata
RBAC v2: only tenant-admin or system-admin can change SLO class and webhook signing config
Audit trail: every delivery attempt is recorded to audit store with actor, outcome, and retry metadata for post-mortem
Potential risk: priority scheduling could be abused to starve lower-tier tenants if misconfigured -- mitigate via fairness caps and telemetry alerts
